newsitem.title: CANADA: Arakis drills four Sudan development wells. [CORRECTED 18:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Arakis drills four Sudan development wells. [CORRECTED 18:55 GMT]

text.p: Arakis Energy Corp said on Monday it completed four development wells on its Sudan oil concessions with productive capabilities ranging from 300 to 4,000 barrels per day. (Corrects production capability range)
Arakis said the wells, drilled during Sudan's rainy season, would optimize production from its Heglig field in the southern part of the country.

The company said casing was run in its Heglig 87a development well, drilled to a depth of 7,015 feet. It said the Bentiu I geological zone tested at 845 barrels per day and the Aradeiba A zone tested at 250 barrels per day.
The well's production capability was estimated at 4,000 barrels per day and new reserves may be booked as a result of the well, the company said.

Another well, Barki 58b, located 1.5 km southeast of the company's Barki 37d discovery well, was drilled to a depth of 7,694 feet. The Bentiu zone tested at 1,000 barrels per day through a 11 mm choke, Arakis said.
It said the well also encountered a 13-foot Aradeiba zone testing at 100 barrels per day.
Arakis said its Kanga 45b well had a production capability of 300 barrels per day and its Kanga West 45c well pumped oil and water and was not viewed as currently commercial.
The company plans to start its 1997 drilling program in mid-December with a well at El Saqr, 25 km from the Heglig base camp, it said. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
